slides.title: ARF: Revised Jones Criteria
slides.subtitle: Master the 2015 updates for NEET-PG & INI-CET

slides.title: JONES
slides.subtitle: 5 Major Criteria for Acute Rheumatic Fever
points: J - Joint involvement (polyarthritis; monoarthritis or polyarthralgia in mod/high-risk)
O - Carditis (clinical OR subclinical echocardiographic valvulitis)
N - Nodules (subcutaneous, firm, painless over extensor surfaces)
E - Erythema marginatum (pink, serpiginous, spares face, non-pruritic)
S - Sydenham chorea (late feature; purposeless movements, hypotonia)
slides.highlight: Exam pearl: Subclinical carditis on echo is now a Major criterion!

slides.title: Low vs Mod/High-Risk Populations
slides.subtitle: Low-Risk || Mod/High-Risk (India)
points: Major Joint: Polyarthritis only || Polyarthritis, polyarthralgia, monoarthritis
Minor Joint: Polyarthralgia || Monoarthralgia
Fever cut-off: >=38.5°C || Fever cut-off: >=38.0°C
ESR cut-off: >=60 mm/hr || ESR cut-off: >=30 mm/hr
slides.highlight: CRP >=3.0 mg/dL (or >ULN) applies to BOTH risk groups

slides.title: Minor Criteria & GAS Proof
points: 4 Minor criteria: Fever, arthralgia, raised ESR/CRP, prolonged PR interval
Prolonged PR: Counts only if carditis is NOT used as a Major criterion
Same joint rule: Don't count joint symptoms in both Major and Minor
GAS evidence: Positive throat culture, RADT, or elevated/rising ASO/anti-DNase B
slides.highlight: ASO peaks at 3–6 weeks; anti-DNase B helps if ASO is negative

slides.title: Diagnostic Rules: Initial vs Recurrent
points: Initial ARF: 2 Major OR 1 Major + 2 Minor (+ GAS evidence)
Recurrent ARF: 2 Major OR 1 Major + 2 Minor OR 3 Minor (+ GAS evidence)
Most common Major sign overall: Migratory polyarthritis (~75%)
Valves affected: Mitral valve most common, followed by aortic valve
slides.highlight: Red flag: Treat strep pharyngitis within 9 days to prevent ARF

slides.title: 3 Classic Jones Exceptions
points: Sydenham chorea: Diagnoses ARF alone (rule out other causes); GAS may be normal
Indolent carditis: Alone diagnoses ARF (rule out other causes); GAS may be absent
Recurrent ARF: 3 Minor criteria suffice if GAS infection is proven
Chorea timing: Appears 1–6 months post-GAS as a late manifestation
slides.highlight: Exam pearl: Chorea & indolent carditis don't require GAS proof

slides.title: High-Yield Exam Takeaways
slides.subtitle: Quick revision before your test
points: India = Mod/High risk: Lower cut-offs (Fever >=38°C, ESR >=30 mm/hr)
Monoarthritis & polyarthralgia are Major criteria in Mod/High risk
Subclinical carditis on Doppler echo counts as Major carditis
slides.highlight: Exam pearl: Joint involvement in ARF shows dramatic response to aspirin

caption:
Still confusing Low-risk vs High-risk Jones Criteria cut-offs? Let’s fix that in 60 seconds.

The 2015 AHA revision changed how we diagnose Acute Rheumatic Fever—especially in moderate/high-risk countries like India:
• Remember the JONES mnemonic for the 5 Major criteria
• Spot the exact Fever, ESR, and Joint cut-offs for India
• Revise subclinical carditis and the 3 classic exam exceptions

Quick PYQ check: Which valve is most commonly involved in acute rheumatic carditis? Drop your answer below!

Slide 4: Changed 'rising ASO/anti-DNase B' to 'elevated/rising ASO/anti-DNase B' because a single elevated titer above age-specific ULN also qualifies as GAS evidence.
Slide 6: Added '(rule out other causes)' to the Sydenham chorea and indolent carditis exception points per AHA 2015 criteria.
